\section{Reproduced methods}
\label{sec:S2}
\textbf{Specifications.} Each method was specified in writing before its code was run: the paper's own choices, the details the paper leaves open (``fills'', each with a reason), the sampling rate, the decision rule of the native mode and a sanity check. Later amendments are appended to the same files with their date and reason. The files are:
\input{generated/supp_specs.tex}
\textbf{Run-to-run variation.} Training of the neural reproductions of Key and Afrasiabi is not bit-reproducible. Two runs on identical folds differ on \runDiffKey{} (Key) and \runDiffAfr{} (Afrasiabi) of \runKeysKey{} (seed, fold, trace) decisions; the paper uses the second run for every row of Table~A. The comparison of Afrasiabi with and without the CT compensation stage in the notes of Table~S1 mixes the two runs and is of the size of this variation; it supports only the statement that the stage is nearly inactive on these traces.

\textbf{Operating conditions that disadvantage a method.} The lumped plants carry little energy above \hfLimit\,kHz (no winding capacitances), which limits the high-frequency detectors of Sim\~oes et al.\ and Ngaopitakkul and Kunakorn; the detector of the latter passes its sanity check on noise-free currents but not on CT secondaries with measurement noise. The feature stage of Abdusalam et al.\ needs \latAbd\,ms per window against a \latAbdBudget\,ms budget (not real-time on the development PC). These conditions are reported, not corrected.

\section{Order of decisions and analyses}
\label{sec:S8}
Decision rules were fixed in a dated plan before each analysis (\texttt{BENCHMARK\_FAIRNESS\_PLAN.md}, with the git history of the repository as the time record; progress log \texttt{IMPLEMENTATION\_PLAN.md}). The hypotheses and decision tables for the reproductions, the statistics and the conventional baselines were committed before any reproduction was evaluated, and were not edited afterwards. The following analyses were added after earlier results had been seen and are labelled post-hoc in the paper: the comparison of every instance with the tuned harmonic 87T and the range-only wording for it; the B2 comparisons with the deployed instance; the gated-only ablation; the extension of the harmonic grid of the tuned 87T to \nGridX{} settings, with its decision rules (restate the claim if the tuned relay is not significantly less dependable than the deployed instance; report a new boundary as unresolved, no second extension) fixed before its run, and every comparison with the relay tuned on it, including its frozen-setting scoring on the shifted-range set and on plant~B; the extension of the claim to the like-for-like mode; the re-measurement of the latency of Alhamd's trained configurations; and the larger training budget of Alhamd's reproduction (both budgets are reported). Some review sections of the plan were committed together after the results they discuss; their timing rests on the dated log.

\section{Audit}
\label{sec:S9}
An independent audit (\texttt{audit/} in the repository) recomputed every reported test from the per-trace files, re-tested them with the trace-clustered permutation test used in the paper, checked the code for leakage (grouping, scaling, threshold selection, use of ground truth at test time) and verified every reference against a publisher record. Its findings that affect the paper are taken in: the test unit, the window stride of the deployed instance (\strideDep{} against \strideBtwo{} in B2), the non-nested B2 search, the subsampling of SVM and random forest, the label definition from the applied fault time, and the classifier-alone path being switched off by the plateau rule in \soloOff{} of \nFoldModels{} CV fold-models.
